text:
The forward‑scattering amplitude is  

\[
f(0)=\frac{1}{2ik}\sum_{l}(2l+1)\big(e^{2i\delta_l}-1\big)
\]

so its imaginary part is  

\[
\operatorname{Im}f(0)=\frac{1}{2k}\sum_{l}(2l+1)\big[1-\cos(2\delta_l)\big]
      =\frac{1}{k}\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\!\delta_l .
\]

Using the given phase shifts (degrees)  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin^{2}\delta_0 &=1,\\
\sin^{2}\delta_1 &\approx0.848,\\
\sin^{2}\delta_2 &\approx0.671,\\
\sin^{2}\delta_3 &=0.250,\\
\sin^{2}\delta_4 &\approx0.0506 .
\end{aligned}
\]

Weighting with \(2l+1\) and summing:

\[
\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_l
=1(1)+3(0.848)+5(0.671)+7(0.250)+9(0.0506)
\approx 9.104 .
\]

For a 50 MeV electron the (non‑relativistic) momentum is  

\[
p=\sqrt{2m_e T}\approx\sqrt{2(0.511\;\text{MeV})(50\;\text{MeV})}\approx7.15\;\text{MeV}/c .
\]

Hence  

\[
k=\frac{p}{\hbar c}= \frac{7.15}{197.327}\;\text{fm}^{-1}\approx 0.0362\;\text{fm}^{-1}.
\]

Finally  

\[
\operatorname{Im}f(0)=\frac{1}{k}\,9.104\approx\frac{9.104}{0.0362}\;\text{fm}
\approx 2.51\times10^{2}\;\text{fm}=251.3\;\text{fm}.
\]

Thus the imaginary part of the forward‑direction scattering amplitude is  

**Answer: A**.
